Changelog

Mirrored from apps/email/CHANGELOG.md, where releases update it. The component's page is email. This page describes the current main branch of MixOS.

Unreleased

  • Keep compose-only restore offers in the owning window across refreshes. Later and the final Discard start the requested blank message; file launches suppress kept-draft offers for that run without deleting saved drafts.

  • Quit waits quietly for closed windows' Save As writes. Cancel revokes prior quit permission and deferred owner close; both empty and object Quit bodies return the same fields and publish the registry execution.

  • Batch mixed mailbox drops into one composer and register document drops by the returned read ticket. Test the existing closed-composer label on a late drop failure and check literal source label keys against the English catalogue.

  • Refuse window on compose, reply and forward, which always create windows; stamp opened window names only on compose-opening command replies.

  • Fix mailbox Quit with simultaneous composer input, retain pending Save As writes through Close and Quit, and carry completed send/save outcomes to the mailbox. Only Cancel on a Quit question revokes a deferred owner close.

  • Return the opened window from Bus compose, reply, forward, document opens and compose.new. Default targeting follows the latest creation or focus; refuse unknown and non-string window targets. Report draft questions from email.quit and paint Bus-created composers immediately.

  • Attach ordinary Markdown to its drop target, open composers for ordinary mailbox file drops, and retire failed document-loading children. Offer kept drafts in compose-only startup and set child app IDs explicitly.

  • Replace the modal composer with one window per message, with File, Edit, Attachments and View menus in its chrome. Add email --compose [FILE.md] and single-instance forwarding through the citizen probe.

  • Give each composer independent drafts, document operations, attachments, Bus targeting (window) and saved placement (compose-<n>). Toolkit drive commands use viewport, including compose menus.

  • Retain the first native window as process owner while children remain; never promote or rename a child into its surface. Close waits for children; Quit asks per draft and supports cancellation.

  • Create and retire composers through a one-off native paint request when the mailbox is parked. Direct document sends retain their engine-owned reply state independently of composer lifetimes.

  • Open and save inert mail documents from compose's File menu (Ctrl+O, Ctrl+Shift+S), with replace questions and background file I/O. Remember the Open/Save folder for the session, initially XDG Documents or Home.

  • Accept document paths on email.compose and email.send; refuse mixed inline fields, unowned From/Reply-To identities and each format error with distinct codes. Drops open mail documents and never send them; other Markdown stays an attachment while composing. Drafts remain private JSON.

  • Send Reply-To and ordered References, including through inline Bus sends.

  • Pin received attachments below the reader body, with a remembered expanded tile view, Save All/Open All, per-file Open/Save and transfer status. Message › Attachments now toggles the bar's expansion.

  • Show attached PNG, JPEG, GIF (first frame) and WebP images after the text by default. View › Show Attachments Inline is remembered across restarts. Previews use capped downloads, two background decode slots, explicit image limits and textures kept only for the open email; remote URLs stay unfetched.

  • Report attachment bar choices and each preview's state/reason in email.info under mail.reader; both choices work through email.execute.

  • Add an Attachments menu inside compose, with Attach files… (Ctrl+Shift+A), Remove all attachments and a one-click paperclip button. The shared chooser runs above compose and remembers the last attachment directory this session.

  • Add email.compose.attachment.add {paths} and dropped-file attachment entry. They share atomic path validation, deduplication, draft revisions, metadata refresh and size warnings; sending refuses changes.

  • Use citizen's shared app-launch helper when opening Prefs, preserving app refusals and avoiding repeated commands after an uncertain outcome.

  • email.execute refuses mail.send when final validation prevents queueing, returning the compose error rather than a successful executed reply.

  • Compose attachment metadata keeps the plain basename in name and the qualified display text in label. Failed sends clear their audit origin.

  • Mixed local/drive input passes retain the drive caller and request id in send audits, with mixed_input=true recording the ambiguity. Other send audits use mixed_input=false.

  • Narrow chip labels retain at least four em of width and truncate their text.

  • Attachment chips wrap within the compose form's field width. Scoped chip frames no longer expand the row and dialog instead of starting a new row.

  • email.send and email.compose accept an optional attachments list of absolute file paths. Symlinks are followed; relative paths, non-files, unreadable files and oversized messages have distinct refusal codes.

  • Send reads files at send time and emits multipart MIME with desktop MIME types, base64 and RFC 2231 filenames. The encoded message is limited by JMAP maxSizeUpload, or 25 MiB when the server advertises no limit.

  • Local drafts save and restore attachment paths (never file contents), including across restarts. Older drafts still load without attachments.

  • Send resolves an earlier uncertain submission before checking local files or upload limits. Attachment reads and encoding run off the async runtime; command validation uses metadata only, and MIME bytes are rendered once.

  • Standalone MIME builders impose no upload limit; Send applies the server's limit to the exact encoded bytes.

  • Sends with attachments log the caller key and paths in the Email app. Person-initiated sends use window; mail.send through email.execute retains the Bus caller. Driven sends retain the actual replayed request id and caller through compose state and queued work for audit correlation.

  • Compose shows attachment chips under Subject with names, sizes, file status, removal and a total. Missing, unreadable and invalid files or an oversized encoded message disable Send. Chips wrap, preserve text line height and disambiguate colliding filenames with their parent directories. Oversize warnings appear on the total line, with distinct account/default limits. Files are checked on open, removal, send failure and before Send; text edits update the estimate from cached sizes without polling files.

  • email.info and the compose reply include the attachment metadata, total, warning and Send enablement. email.compose.attachment.remove {path} removes a path through the same state mutation as the chip's remove button.

  • Attachment-only drafts are kept too. Restoring a vanished file preserves its path and shows it as missing; draft schema 1 remains compatible.

  • Invalid logging configuration reports its error and lets the GUI start without a subscriber.

  • MIME size estimates reserve the maximum 255-byte media type per part, without loading the MIME database or reading file contents. Send restores name/content sniffing on its worker; estimates bound actual MIME size with under 300 bytes of headroom per part.
